content: Former Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China subversion case: Li Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, who pleaded not guilty, have completed 24 days of trial and will face judgment on Friday, August 21. Chow Hang-tung, the former vice-chairperson of the Hong Kong Alliance, represented herself as a barrister in this case. In prison, without a computer or internet access, she handwrote several hundred pages of submissions. At her request, the court played in full two years of June 4th candlelight vigils, recreating the candlelight scenes in Victoria Park and the testimonies of June 4th witnesses. "I am the last defendant, and also the last vice-chair of the Alliance, the first defendant in this case... I am now 41 years old, a barrister, and there isn't much else simple about my background," Chow Hang-tung said with a smile at the start. During her six days of testimony, she smiled from time to time, but also shed tears on several occasions. What do the June 4th vigil and ending one-party dictatorship mean to Chow Hang-tung? What was her 'intent'? This episode of the Podcast continues to take readers to the courtroom, recreating through voice performance Chow Hang-tung's testimony and the cross-examination by the judge and prosecution. Replay: Voice performance — Li Cheuk-yan's testimony: In my heart there is no hostility, only love. Related reports on the Hong Kong Alliance case.
